title: Europe Faces New Wildfire Challenges as Extreme Heat Continues
subtitle: While some fires in France and Spain are now under control, Greece continues to battle dangerous blazes in record-breaking temperatures.

summary.en: Europe is currently dealing with a difficult summer as extreme heat and strong winds fuel dangerous wildfires. While countries like France and Spain have seen progress in controlling their fires, Greece is still fighting to protect coastal areas. Italy is also facing a severe heatwave, with almost all major cities under the highest level of alert. Experts note that Europe is warming faster than any other continent, making these events more frequent. Authorities are urging residents to stay safe as firefighters work to manage the situation.
summary.zh: 歐洲目前正經歷一個艱難的夏天，極端高溫與強風助長了危險的野火。雖然法國與西班牙等國在控制火勢方面已取得進展，但希臘仍在努力保護沿海地區。義大利也面臨嚴重的熱浪侵襲，幾乎所有主要城市都處於最高警戒狀態。專家指出，歐洲的暖化速度比其他任何大陸都快，這使得此類事件發生的頻率更高。當局呼籲居民注意安全，同時消防員正努力控制局勢。

paragraphs.en: Europe is facing a difficult summer as extreme heat and strong winds continue to fuel dangerous wildfires across the continent. While some nations have seen improvements in their fight against the flames, others remain in a state of emergency. According to reports from Al Jazeera English, Greece is currently at the center of a new wildfire crisis. Gale-force winds have fanned flames across several parts of the country, making the work of emergency teams very difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 歐洲正面臨一個艱難的夏天，極端高溫與強風持續助長了橫跨歐陸的危險野火。儘管部分國家在滅火工作上已見改善，但其他地區仍處於緊急狀態。根據半島電視台英語頻道（Al Jazeera English）的報導，希臘目前正處於新一波野火危機的中心。強勁的陣風助長了該國多處的火勢，使得緊急救援團隊的工作變得極為困難。

paragraphs.en: In the region of Viotia, a fire reached the coastal resort of Porto Germeno on Saturday. BBC News reported that hundreds of people, mostly tourists, had to be evacuated by sea to escape the danger. A spokesperson for the fire department told the AFP news agency that homes in the area were certainly damaged. Theodore Giannaros, a wildfire meteorologist at the National Observatory of Athens, described the damage to the area as "inconceivable." The situation has been made worse by winds reaching 130 kilometers per hour, which have prevented some aircraft from dropping water on the fires.
paragraphs.zh: 在維奧蒂亞（Viotia）地區，火勢於週六蔓延至波爾圖格爾梅諾（Porto Germeno）的濱海度假勝地。英國廣播公司新聞網（BBC News）報導，數百名民眾（主要是遊客）必須經由海路撤離以躲避危險。消防部門發言人向法新社（AFP）表示，該地區的民宅確實已受損。雅典國家天文台（National Observatory of Athens）的野火氣象學家狄奧多爾·吉安納羅斯（Theodore Giannaros）形容該地區的損害程度「令人難以想像」。時速高達一百三十公里的強風使情況雪上加霜，導致部分飛機無法進行空中灑水滅火。

paragraphs.en: Across Greece, the fire brigade remains on the highest level of alert. The risk is particularly high in the Attica peninsula and the island of Evia. Sadly, the human cost of these fires has been high, with three firefighters losing their lives so far this summer. The mayor of Thebes, Giorgos Anastasiou, told Open TV that the environmental damage caused by these fires is huge.
paragraphs.zh: 在希臘全國，消防隊仍維持最高警戒層級。阿提卡（Attica）半島與艾維亞島（Evia）的風險尤其高。令人遺憾的是，這些火災已造成慘重的人員傷亡，今年夏天迄今已有三名消防員殉職。底比斯（Thebes）市長喬治斯·阿納斯塔修（Giorgos Anastasiou）向開放電視台（Open TV）表示，這些火災造成的環境破壞極為巨大。

paragraphs.en: While Greece struggles, the situation in other parts of Europe shows signs of improvement. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu stated on Saturday that wildfires in his country are now under control. In the Gironde region, where the largest fire since 1949 recently flared up, the situation has become more stable. According to the BBC, about 200,000 people who were forced to leave their homes in Gironde have now been able to return. In the southeastern Var region, 1,500 firefighters have worked hard to contain the progression of fires, and local officials noted that defensive lines are holding.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管希臘陷入苦戰，歐洲其他地區的情況則出現好轉跡象。法國國防部長塞巴斯蒂安·勒科爾尼（Sebastien Lecornu）週六表示，法國境內的野火目前已受到控制。在發生自一九四九年以來最大火災的吉倫特（Gironde）地區，情況已趨於穩定。根據英國廣播公司報導，先前被迫撤離家園的約二十萬名吉倫特居民，目前已能返回住處。在東南部的瓦爾（Var）地區，一千五百名消防員努力遏止火勢蔓延，當地官員指出，防線目前依然穩固。

paragraphs.en: Similarly, officials in Portugal have declared their major wildfire to be under control. In Spain, while the government declared the end of a national emergency, some hot spots remain. However, most evacuation orders have been lifted, and the largest fires are no longer spreading as they were earlier in the week. Despite this progress, EU data shows that the total land burned in Spain this year is roughly five times higher than the average for this time of year.
paragraphs.zh: 同樣地，葡萄牙官員也宣布該國的主要野火已受到控制。在西班牙，儘管政府宣布國家緊急狀態結束，但仍有部分熱點存在。不過，大多數撤離令已經解除，且規模最大的火災也不再像本週稍早那樣迅速擴散。儘管有所進展，歐盟的數據顯示，西班牙今年燒毀的土地總面積，約為往年同期平均值的五倍。

paragraphs.en: As firefighters battle these blazes, Italy is dealing with a different but related threat: extreme heat. The BBC reports that the Italian health ministry has placed almost all of the country’s major cities on the highest "red" alert for high temperatures. By Monday, 25 out of 27 major cities will be under this warning. Officials are advising residents to stay indoors, avoid direct sunlight during the hottest hours of the day, and drink plenty of fluids to stay healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 在消防員對抗這些火勢的同時，義大利正處理另一項相關威脅：極端高溫。英國廣播公司報導，義大利衛生部已將該國幾乎所有主要城市列為高溫「紅色」最高警戒。到了週一，二十七個主要城市中將有二十五個處於此警告之下。官員建議居民待在室內，避免在一天中最炎熱的時段直接曝曬於陽光下，並多補充水分以維持健康。

paragraphs.en: This extreme heat is being caused by a subtropical anticyclone—a large area of high air pressure that brings hot, dry air—moving in from North Africa. Experts from the European Union’s Copernicus climate service explain that Europe is the fastest-warming continent on Earth. Since the 1980s, it has been heating at more than twice the global average. This trend makes vegetation drier and more likely to catch fire, which allows blazes to spread much faster than in the past.
paragraphs.zh: 這波極端高溫是由來自北非的副熱帶反氣旋（一種帶來炎熱乾燥空氣的高氣壓區）所引起。歐盟哥白尼氣候變化服務（Copernicus Climate Change Service）的專家解釋，歐洲是地球上暖化速度最快的大陸。自一九八零年代以來，歐洲的升溫速度超過全球平均值的兩倍。這種趨勢使植被變得更加乾燥，更容易引發火災，進而導致火勢蔓延的速度遠快於過去。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the combination of high temperatures and dry conditions continues to put pressure on Europe’s water supplies and emergency services. While the immediate danger in some countries has eased, authorities remain cautious. The ongoing crisis serves as a reminder of the challenges that many European nations face as they adapt to a changing climate. For now, the focus remains on keeping people safe and preventing further destruction to homes and the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，高溫與乾燥氣候的結合，持續對歐洲的水資源供應與緊急服務造成壓力。雖然部分國家的立即危險已減輕，但當局仍保持謹慎。這場持續中的危機提醒了許多歐洲國家，在適應氣候變遷的過程中必須面對種種挑戰。目前，重點仍放在確保民眾安全，並防止民宅與環境遭受進一步的破壞。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To increase or strengthen something, especially something bad like a fire or a conflict.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 助長、加劇（尤指火勢或衝突）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（燃料），這裡作動詞用。文中：extreme heat and strong winds continue to fuel dangerous wildfires across the continent.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make a fire burn more strongly by blowing air on it.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（扇子），這裡作動詞用，形容風讓火勢變大。文中：Gale-force winds have fanned flames across several parts of the country, making the work of emergency teams very difficult.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To suddenly start or become much worse.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （火勢、衝突或疾病）突然爆發或惡化。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語形容火勢突然變大，而非字面上的「閃光」。文中：In the Gironde region, where the largest fire since 1949 recently flared up, the situation has become more stable.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To remain effective or strong without breaking or giving way.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（拿著），這裡指防線成功抵擋火勢。文中：1,500 firefighters have worked hard to contain the progression of fires, and local officials noted that defensive lines are holding.

quiz.question: What specifically prevented emergency aircraft from assisting with the fires in the Viotia region?

options.A: The coastal location made it impossible for planes to land.
options.B: Extremely high wind speeds reaching 130 kilometers per hour.
options.C: The destruction of local airports by the fire.
options.D: A lack of available water supplies in the coastal resort area.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，文中明確提到「winds reaching 130 kilometers per hour, which have prevented some aircraft from dropping water on the fires」，因此風速過快是阻礙飛機作業的主因。選項 A 與文中提到的撤離方式無關；選項 C 文中並未提及機場損毀；選項 D 雖然提到水資源壓力，但飛機無法執行任務的原因是風力而非缺水。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the state of wildfires in Europe?

options.A: The crisis is currently uniform across every European nation.
options.B: Most European countries have officially declared the end of the wildfire season.
options.C: The severity of the fire situation varies significantly from one country to another.
options.D: Italy is currently the only country experiencing extreme weather conditions.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章透過對比指出，希臘正處於危機中心，而法國、葡萄牙和西班牙的情況已有所好轉，甚至部分居民已能返家，這顯示各國災情嚴重程度不同。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 錯誤，因為西班牙仍有熱點，且氣候變遷持續帶來威脅；選項 D 錯誤，因為義大利面臨的是「極端高溫」而非僅有它面臨極端天氣，其他國家如希臘則在對抗野火。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'eased' mean in the context of the sentence: 'While the immediate danger in some countries has eased, authorities remain cautious'?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，eased 用來形容危險程度降低，即「減輕、緩和」。選項 A 意思完全相反；選項 C 在此語境下不合邏輯，危險不會因為移動而讓當局保持謹慎；選項 D 過於絕對，文中提到當局仍保持謹慎（remain cautious），顯示危險尚未完全消失，只是暫時緩和。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding Europe's current environmental situation?

options.A: The European Union is successfully solving its climate change problems through new technology.
options.B: Wildfires are solely caused by human negligence in coastal resort areas.
options.C: Europe is facing ongoing environmental challenges, such as wildfires and heatwaves, linked to a warming climate.
options.D: The economic impact of wildfires is the main concern for European governments this summer.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文旨在探討歐洲面臨的野火與極端高溫危機，並引用氣候數據指出歐洲暖化速度快於全球平均，這是導致災害惡化的背景。選項 A 與事實不符，文中並未強調科技解決方案；選項 B 將野火歸咎於人為疏忽過於狹隘，忽略了氣候因素；選項 D 雖有提及損害，但並非文章的核心主旨，文章更側重於氣候變遷帶來的長期挑戰與安全威脅。
